## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. ## How to run it

### Other ways to run it

1. Run it as published (fp16, needs ~4 GB, NVIDIA only, from [huggingface.co/docs](https://huggingface.co/docs/diffusers/optimization/mps))
   
   ```sh
   uv run --with torch --with diffusers --with transformers --with accelerate --with safetensors python -c "import torch; from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline; p=StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained('stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5', torch_dtype=torch.float16).to('cuda'); p.enable_attention_slicing(); p('A lighthouse at sunset', height=512, width=512).images[0].save('image.png')"
   ```

Other versions: fp32 (~8 GB, Mac only) `uv run --with torch --with diffusers --with transformers --with accelerate --with safetensors python -c "from diffusers import StableDiffusionPipeline; p=StableDiffusionPipeline.from_pretrained('stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5').to('mps'); p.enable_attention_slicing(); p('A lighthouse at sunset', height=512, width=512).images[0].save('image.png')"` · Q8_0 (SD.CPP --TYPE) (~2.1 GB) `sd-cli -m models/v1-5-pruned-emaonly.safetensors --type q8_0 -p "a lovely cat"`

Official weights and documentation: [huggingface.co/stable-diffusion-v1-5](https://huggingface.co/stable-diffusion-v1-5/stable-diffusion-v1-5)
